corta: the bank of faders runs off the left and right edges and off the bottom — no console body, no room, no operator is ever visible, only the channel strip itself
escena: SCENE (production suite at night, extreme macro): a long bank of identical channel faders fills the action area of the frame, cropped hard left and right. EVERY fader is pulled all the way DOWN to zero — a dead flat line of forty identical caps, their scales unlit. ONE fader, just right of centre, is pushed ALL THE WAY UP: it stands alone above the flat line, its channel strip the only one with a glowing cool blue level showing. The eye lands on that one raised fader first, then reads the dead flat row it is standing in. A hard low raking light from the left skims across the caps and throws a row of sharp parallel shadows; the light dies before it reaches the text area. A small orange sculpture sits at the far right end of the strip, cropped by the edge. 100mm macro lens at f/4, focus on the raised fader. The whole frame is COOL and contemporary: daylight-neutral white balance, blue-leaning shadows, nothing warm, amber, golden or tungsten anywhere, no retro glow — the ONLY warm colour in the entire picture is the small orange sculpture itself. Everything except the sculpture is completely unbranded and no text anywhere is readable: the channel markings are tiny, angled and shallow-focused. CRITICAL FRAMING (vertical 9:16): the ACTION AREA is the band from 40% to 80% of the frame height, measured from the top edge. The TOP 40% of the frame is one single dark, evenly toned surface with NOTHING in it: no object, no screen, no lamp, no window, no light beam, no bright spot, no shadow edge. If a person is in the picture, the top of her head is no higher than 40% down from the top edge. All action, all light and every bright patch stay inside the action area; the bottom of the frame stays calm and dark.

lecho.objeto: the out-of-focus near edge of the console apron running along the very bottom against the lens
